summary: Dedicated customer requests intermittently routed through eu-central egress, causing p90-p99 inference latency regressions
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-09T14:20Z Parcelly reported a sudden p95/p99 regression for generation requests. Impact: ~15% of requests for their dedicated pool in us-east had tail latency spikes from ~180ms to 1.2s, causing client-side timeouts and retries. Environment: Dedicated pool (parcelly-dedicated-01) in us-east using redwood-large-v2. Observed behavior: A subset of inferences were routed via eu-central egress nodes, adding ~800-1,000ms RTT and increasing total token latency. Expected behavior: Requests should remain in-region (us-east) or route to nearest healthy egress without cross-region detours.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use Parcelly API key against production endpoint in us-east. 2) Send 1k concurrent generation requests with typical 512-token prompts and streaming enabled. 3) Observe p50/p95/p99 in Redwood Console per-route latency. 4) Correlate request IDs flagged by customer with edge/egress path in access logs.
logs:
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] request_id=rq_9f8a ... route=us-east -> eu-central-egress node=eg-32 latency=980ms
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] request_id=rq_9f8b ... route=us-east node=us-east-egress latency=120ms
[2026-03-09T14:22:07Z] healthcheck: eu-central-egress status=degraded for cluster=egress-v2 (reason=transient-conn-fail)
[2026-03-09T14:23:12Z] smart-routing: fallbackTriggered=true policy=latencyBudget computedBest=us-east selected=eu-central (cachedPreference=eu-central due to stale affinity)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: a transient degradation in a subset of us-east egress nodes caused the routing controller to fall back to a cached preference that favored eu-central. Evidence: Grafana trace (https://grafana.redwood.com/d/abcd/egress-latency?from=2026-03-09T14:00Z&to=2026-03-09T15:00Z) shows simultaneous health check timeouts for eg-29/eg-31 in us-east. Routing logs show 'cachedPreference' entries created by the affinity cache that have TTL=10m and were not invalidated after node recovery. Network team also observed a short-lived spike in packet loss on the us-east public egress AS path at 2026-03-09T14:18Z (BGP flap reported by cloud provider). Temporary correlation between BGP event and routing cache invalidation race. Repro attempted in staging with canary: forcing healthchecks to flip quickly reproduces cachedPreference not being refreshed; when we add immediate cache invalidation on healthcheck success, cross-region fallback stops. Next steps: create patch to invalidate affinity cache on healthcheck success, increase egress pool headroom for dedicated pools, and schedule a controlled canary rollout. Related: see linked issue SUP-20645 for prior egress fallback occurrences.
comments: 2026-03-09T15:02Z - Support (Liam O'Connor): Acknowledged. Opened investigation and escalated to Routing SRE. Asked for request IDs and sample traces from Parcelly.
2026-03-09T15:20Z - Parcelly (customer): Sent sample request_ids: rq_9f8a,rq_9f9c,rq_a01f. Noting retries at client because of 2x timeout at 1s. Impacting checkout flow.

2026-03-09T16:05Z - Routing SRE (Marisol Vega): Found BGP flap from provider at 2026-03-09T14:18Z. us-east eg-29/31 marked unhealthy briefly; affinity cache kept preference to eu-central for ~7min. Draft fix: invalidate cache immediately when healthcheck recovers. Will run canary patch.

2026-03-09T17:40Z - Support (Asha Patel): Applied emergency config change to disable cross-region fallback for dedicated pools while patch is validated. This reduced error count for Parcelly; monitoring continuing.

2026-03-10T09:15Z - Engineering (Diego Ramos): Canary shows drop in cross-region routed requests from 12% to <0.5% for parcelly-dedicated-01. Preparing PR for cache invalidation and a follow-up to reduce affinity TTL.
resolution: Mitigation: temporarily disabled cross-region fallback for dedicated pools and added emergency rule to prefer in-region egress. Permanent fix: merged PR to invalidate affinity cache on healthcheck success and lowered affinity TTL from 10m to 90s. Rollout: canary on 2026-03-10 (passed), full rollout scheduled 2026-03-12 after additional verification. Customer workaround: Parcelly increased client-side timeout to 2.5s during incident window. Follow-up actions: postmortem, add alert when cross-region route percentage >1% for dedicated pools, update runbook with cache invalidation step.
notes: Postmortem link pending; assigned follow-up owner: Marisol Vega.
